headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via shared Dify datastore and Haystack MCP/network paths; cascading errors are also plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify explicitly has shared state via the Dify server datastore and can ingest uploaded knowledge-base files; Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is inferred, not directly reproduced, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are routed into Haystack prompts or MCP inputs without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF shared datastore content is rendered as instructions by either agent, prompt hijack becomes feasible.
mitigations: Add a strict content-delimiter template between agents.
Strip tool directives from inter-agent text before forwarding.
Require provenance labels on all shared datastore entries.
Disable MCP routes that accept free-form agent text.
requires-engineering: add policy-based prompt firewalling.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge-base content and conversation logs, while Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and can call REST/MCP endpoints with broad egress. If the pair shares workspace or passes file contents through prompts, sensitive Dify data can leak into Haystack outputs or external calls. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF Dify conversation logs or KB files are forwarded to Haystack, leakage occurs.
IF Haystack sends retrieved context to external APIs, any imported Dify data can exit the boundary.
mitigations: Minimize fields forwarded from Dify to Haystack.
Redact secrets from KB and logs before handoff.
Restrict Haystack outbound endpoints to allowlisted hosts.
Separate credentials for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses; Haystack can use MCP and broad network egress. Even without explicit shared-write claims for Haystack, overlapping mutable surfaces through tools and external services can conflict when both operate on the same resources. Because Haystack’s write scope is not documented, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same external resource through tools or MCP, race conditions can occur.
IF Dify writes artifacts that Haystack later mutates via an API, state conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Disable concurrent mutation of shared resources.
Use optimistic-lock tokens on shared records.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform and Haystack is a search-RAG system, so a common pattern is Dify producing prompts or retrieved context that Haystack then consumes. If Haystack treats Dify output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or responses. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Dify-generated text is fed into Haystack without validation, errors can propagate.
IF Haystack uses Dify outputs as retrieval truth, downstream answers may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.
Require citations for any factual claim passed onward.
Flag low-confidence outputs before handoff.
Limit Haystack to retrieval-only mode for Dify inputs.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify handles knowledge-base content, conversation logs, and secrets, while Haystack only documents anonymous usage statistics. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so a compliance breach is not established. The main issue is a documented gap in evidence rather than a proven policy conflict, which fits low.
conditions: IF Dify data includes regulated content and Haystack is deployed under a stricter residency or retention policy, a mismatch may arise.
IF Haystack is configured to retain imported Dify content longer than Dify expects, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before handoff.
Avoid sending regulated data to Haystack.
Document retention for shared artifacts.
Review deployment region settings.
requires-engineering: align DPA and retention controls.
